title: Carolina Vinegar Pulled Pork
seoTitle: Carolina Vinegar Pulled Pork | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: All-day smoke that turns into the easiest line service
subtitle: Shoulder smoke, tangy mop sauce, and a slaw bar for ten sandwiches
description: Pork shoulder rides low and slow, gets mopped with a Carolina vinegar sauce, then pulled into a pan of drippings. Build-your-own sandwiches with slaw and pickles.

steps.title: Season the shoulder
steps.instruction: Coat shoulder with mustard binder. Mix salt, pepper, paprika, brown sugar, and garlic powder; rub all over. Let sit 20 minutes while smoker heats.

steps.title: Smoke low and steady
steps.instruction: Heat smoker to 250°F. Smoke shoulder fat side up until bark is dark and the internal temp reaches about 165°F, 5–7 hours. Spritz with water if the surface looks dry.

steps.title: Mix the vinegar mop
steps.instruction: Whisk vinegar, water, hot sauce, flakes, sugar, and salt. Reserve 1/3 cup clean for finishing; use the rest for mopping and pulling.

steps.title: Wrap and finish
steps.instruction: Wrap tightly in foil. Return to smoker (or a 275°F oven) until the probe slides in like butter and the internal temp is 203–205°F, about 2–3 hours.

steps.title: Rest, then pull
steps.instruction: Rest wrapped 45 minutes. Pour juices into a pan. Pull pork, discarding large fat pieces. Stir in a few ladles of juices plus the reserved clean vinegar sauce to taste.

steps.title: Tonight’s board
steps.instruction: Pan of pulled pork, buns, slaw, pickles, and extra vinegar sauce. Call it out on the board so the crew can build fast and get back on shift.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Reheat covered with a splash of water or sauce. Use in nachos, tacos, or loaded baked potatoes.

proTips: If the bark is right, wrap—don’t chase a specific hour count.
Resting is not optional; it keeps pulled pork juicy and easier to shred.
Finishing with a clean sauce gives punch without raw-meat risk.
tonightSpread: Pulled pork in a hotel pan with ladle, buns stacked, slaw + pickles on ice.
Optional: set out mustard and hot sauce so everyone can tune their sandwich.
leftovers: Pulled pork quesadillas with cheddar and jalapeños.
BBQ pork fried rice with scallions and scrambled eggs.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It feeds a crowd, holds forever, and tastes even better after it rests. works for a crew meal where calls might interrupt the cook.
mealPrepNotes: Start early. Once pulled, hold covered at 170°F for 2 hours with a splash of vinegar sauce. If the smoker schedule slips, wrap earlier and finish in the oven.
substitutions: No smoker? Use a 275°F oven and add 1 tsp liquid smoke to the vinegar sauce. Finish the same temps.
Swap buns for tortillas and run it as taco night.
